name: Shared memories 2002: six CCW circumcerebral patterns for the exposed partner (30 min)
origin: Persinger lab, Laurentian University (Persinger, Cook & Tiller 2002; Booth, Charette & Persinger 2002)
summary: A reconstruction of what the field-exposed partner received in two 2002 Persinger-lab studies of emotionally related pairs: six counter-clockwise circumcerebral patterns (here the lab's burst-firing and Thomas battery of the same year, 5 min each) while the other partner, in another room, wrote about a randomly chosen stimulus. Persinger's lab reported significant blind matching of the partners' texts for 5 of 7 analysable pairs and accuracy that varied with geomagnetic activity.
notes: Persinger, Cook & Tiller had 44 students blind-match each exposed partner's narrative with the related partner's concurrent comments on a randomly selected stimulus (significant for 5 of 7 analysable pairs; congruence correlated rho = -.72 with geomagnetic activity over the 24 h of the session). Booth, Charette & Persinger exposed the female member of 15 emotionally involved pairs, double-blind as to field or sham, to 'six different patterns' of 'counterclockwise weak magnetic fields' while the male member wrote the memories one of five postcards evoked; ranking accuracy rose with the global K index (0-5). The abstracts give only 'temporal configurations in the order of 20 msec'. The six configurations here are Table 1 of the same lab's Swann paper of the same year (Cook and Tiller co-authored both; it calls them 'our standard protocol'), 5 min each (an assumption; 30 min in the companion studies): point duration 1, 1, 3 ms, silence between repeats 1, 1, 3000 ms, time on the first coil 20, 100, 200 ms and change per coil +2, +20, -2, for the burst-firing (B) and again the Thomas (T) rows. The signs are read literally: each next coil gets 2 ms more in the +2 rows (20 to 34 ms), 20 ms more in the +20 rows (100 to 240 ms) and 2 ms less in the -2 rows (200 to 186 ms). Persinger & Lavallee 2010 use '+' to mean shorter, which would give 20 to 6 ms and 200 to 214 ms; the literal reading was chosen because the +20 rows cannot shorten seven times from 100 ms, Cook 1999's full turns of about 200 to 2000 ms fit it better (216 ms per turn at 20 to 34 ms, 104 ms at 20 to 6 ms), and the Koren software patent (US 6,312,376) uses the plain sign. The schedule the lab actually ran was never published. The Thomas pattern is the exact 849-point patent table; the burst-firing values were never published, so the built-in accelerating burst (230 points, 6-30 Hz at 3 ms, 18-90 Hz when played at 1 ms) stands in. Coil 1 left frontal, counter-clockwise seen from above, coil 8 right prefrontal (Persinger & Lavallee 2010): Fp1, FT7, TP7, O1, O2, TP8, FT8, Fp2. The intensity is not in the abstracts; 1 uT follows the lab's paired studies (the Swann exposure used 2-5 uT). persinger-swann-2002-table1 runs the same table at 3.5 uT; persinger-six-config-battery-2008 (2008 table, 5 uT) runs a related battery. Cautions: the geomagnetic correlation runs in opposite directions in the two papers, and blind matching of free text is weak evidence. Single-lab claims, never independently replicated; independent double-blind tests of God-Helmet-type fields found no field effect (Granqvist 2005; Gendle & McGrath 2012). Score blind and never use results for decisions about real people. Not for people with epilepsy or a seizure history; stop on distress.
setting: Exposed partner: seated and blindfolded with the helmet in a quiet, dark room. Other partner: a separate room, no helmet, writing the memories evoked by one of five postcards that someone else picked at random. Afterwards the cards are ranked (Booth et al.) or the two texts matched by judges who do not know the card (Persinger et al.). Log the planetary K index for the session time, as the lab did.
schedule: One session per pair in the originals. For a self-test, randomise field and sham sessions with the app's Blind option and fix the scoring rule in advance.
source: Persinger, Cook & Tiller 2002, Enhancement of images of possible memories of others during exposure to circumcerebral magnetic fields: correlations with ambient geomagnetic activity, Percept Mot Skills 95:531-543 https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/12434847/ ; Booth, Charette & Persinger 2002, Ranking of stimuli that evoked memories in significant others after exposure to circumcerebral magnetic fields: correlations with ambient geomagnetic activity, Percept Mot Skills 95:555-558 https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/12434850/ ; Persinger, Roll, Tiller, Koren & Cook 2002, Percept Mot Skills 94:927-949 (Table 1, six configurations) https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/12081299/ ; Persinger & Lavallee 2010, J Conscious Explor Res 1(7):785-807 (coil 1 left frontal; '20+2' notation) https://jcer.com/index.php/jcj/article/view/99 ; Koren & Persinger, US 6,312,376 B1 (sequence interval and sequence acceleration) https://patents.google.com/patent/US6312376B1/en ; Thomas, Prato, Kavaliers & Persinger, US 6,234,953 B1, Table 1 (Thomas pulse) https://patents.google.com/patent/US6234953B1/en ; Buckner et al. 2015, PLoS ONE 10(4):e0124136 (Thomas file: 849 points at 3 ms) https://europepmc.org/article/MED/25875081 ; Carniello 2020, PhD thesis, Laurentian University (230-point burst-firing file) https://laurentian.scholaris.ca/items/8c92763c-cd19-4a21-b242-3b572a28ce55 ; Persinger, Koren & Tsang 2003, Percept Mot Skills 97:877 (paired study, 1 uT range) https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/14738355/ ; Cook, Koren & Persinger 1999, Neurosci Lett 268:61-64 https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/10400078/ ; Granqvist et al. 2005, Neurosci Lett 379:1 https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/15849873/ ; Gendle & McGrath 2012, Percept Mot Skills 114:217 https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/22582690/
